concern.concern: Proof 2.1 writes 'x=∑_i(a_i a_i+b_i b_i) with a_i,b_i ∈ F₂', reusing the symplectic basis-vector names as scalar coordinates. The subsequent Gauss-sum calculation is sound, but this coordinate expansion needs distinct scalar names to be well-typed.

original_concerns.reason: The symplectic basis a_i,b_i is already a family of vectors, while the same symbols are then rebound as F2 coordinates; q_F(a_i) would consequently be ill-typed under that binding. Use alpha_i,beta_i for scalar coordinates throughout the expansion and quadratic expression. The subsequent four-term factor is 2(-1)^(q(a_i)q(b_i)), so the Gauss-sum proof and full invariant claim are unchanged.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: 2.1 In a symplectic basis, every vector is uniquely $x=\sum_i(a_i a_i+b_i b_i)$ with $a_i,b_i\in\mathbb F_2$. The refinement identity gives $$q_F(x)=\sum_i\bigl(a_iq_F(a_i)+b_iq_F(b_i)+a_ib_i\bigr).$$ Therefore the finite Gauss sum factors as $$\sum_{x\in H_1(F;\mathbb F_2)}(-1)^{q_F(x)}=\prod_i\sum_{a,b\in\mathbb F_2}(-1)^{a q_F(a_i)+b q_F(b_i)+ab}=2^g(-1)^{\sum_iq_F(a_i)q_F(b_i)}.$$ The left side depends only on $q_F$, not on a basis, so the exponent defining the Arf value is basis-independent. [step 1.1, given, algebra]
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: 2.1 In a symplectic basis, every vector is uniquely $x=\sum_i(\alpha_i a_i+\beta_i b_i)$ with $\alpha_i,\beta_i\in\mathbb F_2$. The refinement identity gives $$q_F(x)=\sum_i\bigl(\alpha_iq_F(a_i)+\beta_iq_F(b_i)+\alpha_i\beta_i\bigr).$$ Therefore the finite Gauss sum factors as $$\sum_{x\in H_1(F;\mathbb F_2)}(-1)^{q_F(x)}=\prod_i\sum_{a,b\in\mathbb F_2}(-1)^{a q_F(a_i)+b q_F(b_i)+ab}=2^g(-1)^{\sum_iq_F(a_i)q_F(b_i)}.$$ The left side depends only on $q_F$, not on a basis, so the exponent defining the Arf value is basis-independent. [step 1.1, given, algebra]
